decisions.question: Question first: where does the setting live?
decisions.default_taken: bottom of the Practice tab, with a one-line pointer under every held question
decisions.why: The app has no settings screen and practice options already live there. Moving it is one block.

decisions.question: Question first: how does the setting persist?
decisions.why: It needs no schema change. Syncing it later means adding one field to the progress row.

decisions.question: Question first: do existing users also get B?
options: B only for new users; existing users keep none
decisions.why: Pavol said B as the default. One tap on the Practice tab sets None.

decisions.question: Form B: must the box be filled before comparing?
options: no, an empty box is allowed
yes, at least a few characters
decisions.why: Typing is never forced on a phone, and the metric can split by wrote.

decisions.question: Form C: how long is the hold?
decisions.why: It matches the mockup Pavol saw. The value is one constant.

decisions.question: Tracking without new event names
options: key_action question_first {mode, wrote?, q, from} + question_first_set {mode, was} + question_first on start_*
decisions.why: The start_* tag lets first-try accuracy be compared by mode against none, which is the signature metric. B's words never leave the device.

commonplace_explainer.text: The commonplace book is your own collection of the law's exact wording. When you answer a verified question, the box under the explanation quotes the sentence from the AI Act or another EU act that settles it. Tap “Copy to my commonplace book” under that passage to keep it. Your passages are on the Guide tab, under “My commonplace book”, filed by act and article. Each one shows the question it came from, and “Copy all as text” exports the lot, so you can reread the real wording before a mock instead of someone's summary.

private_bank.recommendation: Option A (private Chartres/epso-bank, fetched at build with a read-only token), with no history rewrite. The live app bundle carries all 231 questions, and the prerendered pages carry 159 of them (every verified question, plus a 20-question engineering sample), so privacy protects the source files, the verification notes and future drafts, not the content. A rewrite would break commit links and deploy tags for no real gain.
pavol_steps: Create the private repo Chartres/epso-bank, empty.
Say 'go, Option A'. Claude pushes bank/ and verification/ into it, or he runs the four git commands in the plan.
Create a fine-grained token: owner Chartres, only epso-bank, Contents read-only, longest expiry. Note the expiry date.
Add it to epso-kviz → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions as EPSO_BANK_TOKEN (optionally also as a Dependabot secret).
Say the secret is in. Claude opens the switch-over PR (fetch step in CI, bank files gitignored, sample bank, licence text).
Answer the history question: leave it (recommended) or rewrite it (destructive, only on his explicit yes).

listing_draft.where: r/EUCareers wiki, by modmail to the moderators (not verified from here: Reddit returns 403 to automated reads; Pavol checks the wiki page and the self-promotion rule first). Full draft: docs/plans/listing-draft.md
listing_draft.text: EPSO AI Field Trainer (https://epsokviz.dravec.org): free, unofficial practice for EPSO/AD/430/26 Field 1 (Artificial Intelligence). 231 multiple-choice questions across the three Annex II areas (AI engineering, AI Act and governance, EU digital policy), and a mock of 30 questions in 40 minutes. Verbal, numerical and abstract reasoning practice in Czech, Slovak or English. For 139 of the 151 law and policy questions, the answer shows the EUR-Lex passage that settles it; the other 12 are marked as not verified. No sign-up. Made by a candidate in the same competition.
listing_draft.repo_description: Free, unofficial practice trainer for EPSO/AD/430/26 Field 1 (Artificial Intelligence): 231 MCQs (139 law and policy answers checked against the AI Act and other EU acts), a 30-question/40-minute mock, and reasoning tests in Czech, Slovak or English.
